newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-RENTERIA INSIDE-THE-PARK HOMER HELPS REDS PAST MARLINS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-RENTERIA INSIDE-THE-PARK HOMER HELPS REDS PAST MARLINS.

text.p: Edgar Renteria had a game-tying inside-the-park home run in the bottom of the ninth inning and singled in the winning run in the 11th to lift the Florida Marlins to a 4-3 win over the Cincinnati Reds Saturday.
"This was a heck of game," said Marlins manager Jim Leyland. "There were great plays on both sides. If you can't enjoy a game like that, you can't enjoy baseball."

In the 11th, Luis Castillo drew a leadoff walk off Kevin Jarvis (0-1), stole second and advanced to third on catcher Brook Fordyce's errant throw. Renteria followed with a drive over a drawn-in outfield to win the game.
Robb Nen (1-0) worked the 11th to pick up the win for Florida, which halted Cincinnati's streak of 83 straight wins when leading after eight innings.

The Reds took the lead in the seventh when Bret Boone singled with two out off starter Tony Saunders and came home on a double by Fordyce. Jay Powell came on and yielded a single to pinch-hitter Eduardo Perez for a 3-2 Reds edge.

Jeff Shaw came on in the ninth for a save chance, but Renteria hit his first offering to the gap, where right fielder Reggie Sanders and centre fielder Deion Sanders collided, allowing Renteria to circle the bases.

"We both called for it, but we couldn't hear," said Reggie Sanders, who lay on the ground a while after the collision. "Neither of us wanted to pull up and have it drop. The ball was tailing to me so I thought it was mine.
"It was a bang-bang play literally. After the collision, I looked at the scoreboard and said, how did they get three runs?"
"I didn't see it," said Renteria of the collision. "I saw I had a chance for a double, but when I saw them on the ground, I knew I had a home run."

In Houston, Sid Fernandez allowed two runs over five innings and Ramon Garcia worked four scoreless innings for his first National League save to lead the Astros to a 6-2 win over the St Louis Cardinals, who matched the worst start in franchise history.
Fernandez (1-0), limited to 11 starts last season with Philadelphia due to injury, gave up four hits, walked two and struck out three.
Garcia, who spent last season with Milwaukee, allowed three hits and struck out five.

Delino DeShields led off the game with his first home run to give the Cardinals a 1-0 lead. He left in the third inning with a sprained left ankle. X-rays were negative and he is listed as day-to-day.
The Cardinals have opened with five straight losses for the first time since 1973 and the fifth time ever.
In Montreal, Larry Walker hit three solo home runs to burn his former team and four other Colorado Rockies homered in a 15-3 rout of the Expos.
Walker went 4-for-5, drove in five runs and stole a base.

He hit back-to-back homers with Andres Galarraga in the fourth and with Ellis Burks in the sixth. Dante Bichette homered in the second and Vinny Castilla in the seventh as Colorado set a club record for homers in a game.
Walker, who had eight career two-homer games, is batting .476 with six homers and 11 RBI in five games this season.

In San Diego, Sterling Hitchcock allowed just one hit and two baserunners over eight innings in his National League debut and Quilvio Veras had a two-run double in the second as the Padres handed the Philadelphia Phillies their fourth straight loss, 4-1.
Hitchcock (1-0), acquired from Seattle in the off-season for Scott Sanders, allowed one run with a walk and five strikeouts. Trevor Hoffman struck out the side in the ninth for his first save.

In Los Angeles, Francisco Cordova combined with three relievers on a six-hitter and Jermaine Allensworth hit a two-run homer in the first inning as the Pittsburgh Pirates ended the Dodgers' three-game winning streak with a 3-1 win.
Cordova (1-0) became the first Pirates starter to earn a victory, allowing one run and six hits over seven innings with no walks and four strikeouts.

In San Francisco, pinch-hitter Rick Wilkins doubled home the game's only runs in the bottom of the eighth inning and four pitchers combined on a three-hitter as the Giants blanked the sputtering New York Mets, 2-0.

In Atlanta, Javy Lopez drove in two runs and snapped a tie with a fifth-inning double as the Braves held an 8-5 lead over the Chicago Cubs in the bottom of the seventh inning when the game was suspended due to rain.
The game will resume on Sunday afternoon before the scheduled contest.
There were two rain delays totalling three hours, 27 minutes.
